Input and how to call it

A verified example input (it returned data on 2026-10-29):

{
  "queries": [
    "python"
  ],
  "locations": [
    "Bangalore"
  ],
  "companySizes": [
    "small",
    "medium"
  ],
  "includeDescription": true,
  "maxJobsPerQuery": 50
}

One HTTP call starts a run, waits for it and returns the records (token from console.apify.com):

curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/data_daemon~instahyre-jobs-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"queries": ["python"], "locations": ["Bangalore"], "companySizes": ["small", "medium"], "includeDescription": true, "maxJobsPerQuery": 50}'

Python: ApifyClient(token).actor("data_daemon/instahyre-jobs-scraper").call(run_input=...), full file python/instahyre-jobs-scraper.py. Node.js: node/instahyre-jobs-scraper.mjs. n8n: importable workflow.
AI assistant (MCP): add the remote server https://mcp.apify.com/?tools=data_daemon/instahyre-jobs-scraper with header Authorization: Bearer YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN in Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or VS Code and ask for the data in plain words.

All input fields
FieldTypeMeaning
queriesarrayOne Instahyre search per item, matched against job titles and skill tags, e.g. python, react, data science, devops, product management, java developer. Put cities in locations. A job found by two keywords is saved and charged once. Leave the list with one item for a quick first run.
allJobsbooleanIgnore the keywords and deliver every open Instahyre job: a full-board export for job aggregators and tech-hiring trackers (12,724 open jobs on 26 Oct 2026). Instahyre has no date filter, so combine it with Only new jobs since the last run: the first run exports the board and later runs open only the jobs they have not delivered. locations, company size, job type and maxJobs still apply; the per-keyword cap does not. You can also put * in the keywords.
locationsarrayOptional. Cities as Instahyre lists them: Bangalore, Mumbai, Delhi, Gurgaon, Noida, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune, Kolkata, Ahmedabad, or Work From Home for remote roles; regions such as South India and about 300 smaller cities also work. Several cities = any of them. Common alternative spellings (Bengaluru, Gurugram, Bombay, Remote) are mapped; an unknown name is ignored with a note in the status message. Leave empty for all of India.
minExperienceintegerOnly jobs whose stated experience range reaches at least this many years (0-30). Checked on each job page; jobs that state no range are kept.
maxExperienceintegerOnly jobs whose stated experience range starts at or below this many years (0-30). 1 or 2 is a good early-career filter.
experienceYearsintegerInstahyre's own experience filter: only jobs open to a candidate with exactly this many years (the job's range must cover it). Applied by the site before anything is fetched, so it is the cheapest way to narrow a search; combine with minExperience/maxExperience for a band.
postedWithinDaysintegerOnly jobs posted in the last N days (1-365). Instahyre keeps jobs open for months and its search has no date filter, so the Actor reads the posting date from each job page and leaves out older jobs without charging. In only-new mode the jobs that are left out are remembered too, so later runs do not re-check them.
companySizesarrayOptional. Any of small (under 100 employees), medium (100-1,000) and large (over 1,000). Several values = any of them. Applied by the site.
jobTypestringall (default), full-time or internship. Applied by the site.
companiesarrayOptional. Only jobs posted by these companies, e.g. Amazon, Deutsche Telekom Digital Labs. Several names = any of them. Applied by the site; combine with an empty keyword list to watch everything a company posts.
includeDescriptionbooleanOn (default): one extra request per job reads the public job page and adds the full description (HTML and plain text), posting date, experience range, employment type, job functions and the company website. The price per job is the same either way. Off: listing fields only (title, company profile, cities, skills, URL), about three times as fast, enough for counting jobs or sizing a market.
maxJobsPerQueryintegerStop a keyword after this many new jobs (default 50). Cost: $0.0008 per job with its description, so 50 jobs = $0.04. Raise it for full exports: python alone matches about 4,300 open jobs and the site serves 35 per page.
maxJobsintegerHard cap on saved jobs for the whole run across all keywords (0 = no cap).
onlyNewSinceLastRunbooleanOn: deliver only jobs that an earlier run with the same stateName has not already delivered, and skip the rest without charging. Set maxJobsPerQuery high enough for the first run to take the whole result list (or add postedWithinDays), so later runs really return only new postings. Off (default): return every matching job.
stateNamestringOptional name for this search's memory when onlyNewSinceLastRun is on, e.g. python-bangalore-daily. Leave empty to derive it from the keywords, cities and filters. Use a new name to start over.
skipJobIdsarrayArray of job IDs you already have (the id field from earlier runs), e.g. ["424473", "441980"]. They are skipped before any page fetch and never charged. Large arrays are fine.

Price
$0.0008 per job ($0.80 per 1,000); $0.001 per run. List prices for Apify Free and Starter plans; Scale and Business plans pay 15% to 30% less.

Job$0.0008$0.80One job with its full description: title, company profile, experience range, skills, functions, locations, posted date, job URL.
Actor Start$0.001Charged when the Actor starts running. Number of events charged depends on Actor memory (one event per GB, minimum one event).
Worked example: the input above, capped at 50 jobs, costs at most $0.041. Apify's free plan includes $5 of usage a month, about 6,250 jobs; the Actor's own compute is included in the per-record price, and records skipped by filters, de-duplication or only-new mode are not charged.

What it is not for
Non-tech roles (IIMJobs, Foundit); salary bands (Instahyre does not publish pay); applicant counts (Hirist, IIMJobs). The data belongs to its publisher; the Actor reads public pages and endpoints and leaves out personal contact details.

Questions buyers ask
How much does it cost to scrape Instahyre?
$0.0008 per job with its full description plus $0.001 per run, so 100 jobs cost about $0.08 and a 50-jobs-a-day feed about $1.25 a month.
Is there an official Instahyre API?
No public one. This Actor reads the JSON that the Instahyre website itself loads for its job search, plus the public job pages, and exposes them as a REST API with schedules, webhooks and only-new-jobs runs.
Does it return the full job description?
Yes, as HTML and plain text, plus the experience range, posting date, job functions, skills and the company profile with headcount, founding year and website.
Why is the posting date old on many jobs?
Instahyre keeps a job open until the employer closes it, so a feed without postedWithinDays includes jobs posted months ago. Use postedWithinDays for recent postings, or only-new mode, which after the first run delivers only jobs that are new on the site.
Does it include salaries or applicant counts?
No. Instahyre does not publish salary ranges or applicant counts on public job pages, and this Actor only reads public data.
Why does a city return nothing?
The site only accepts the location names it lists; the Actor maps the common alternative spellings and names any location it had to ignore in the status message. Use Bangalore, Delhi, Gurgaon, Noida, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune, Kolkata, Ahmedabad or Work From Home.
Do I need a proxy or login?
No.

Instahyre websiteCandidate and employer accountsNo export or API; salary and applicant counts are not shown publicly anywhere
Hirist or IIMJobs APIs (same publisher)Applicant counts and salary bandsDifferent boards; Instahyre is the one with company headcount and size filters
Other Instahyre Actors on Apify StoreSame boardCompare price per 1,000, company-profile fields and only-new mode

# Luma (lu.ma) events as JSON API | Daemon Data

Source: https://datadmon.github.io/actors/luma-events-scraper/

Luma (lu.ma) events as JSON API

Luma Events Scraper is a pay-per-record Apify Actor by Daemon Data that returns lu.ma events by city, category, keyword or calendar: dates, venue, tickets, hosts as JSON, CSV or Excel. It costs $0.0015 per event with the default options ($1.50 per 1,000); no login to the source site, no proxy, no browser, and the same input runs from the Apify console, one REST call, Python, Node.js, n8n or an AI assistant through MCP.

Daemon Data Luma Events Scraper on Apify   Listing as plain text

Checked on 19 Oct 2026, on the Apify platform
San Francisco listed 105 upcoming events; three cities (San Francisco, New York, London) gave 100 events with full details in 36 seconds for $0.15 plus the $0.001 start fee. The default run (the 25 soonest San Francisco events with details) takes about 10 seconds and costs $0.04.

Founders, investors and community managersTrack what the ecosystem is doing this week: founder dinners, demo days, hackathons, workshops; follow specific calendars (lu.ma/<organiser>) and get new events the morning they are published.

One HTTP call starts a run, waits for it and returns the records (token from console.apify.com):

curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/data_daemon~luma-events-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

Python: ApifyClient(token).actor("data_daemon/luma-events-scraper").call(run_input=...), full file python/luma-events-scraper.py. Node.js: node/luma-events-scraper.mjs. n8n: importable workflow.

All input fields
FieldTypeMeaning
citiesarrayLuma discover cities, e.g. San Francisco, New York, London, Berlin, Bengaluru, Tokyo, Singapore (87 cities; a lu.ma/<city> URL or a discplace-... id works too). One upcoming-events feed per city, newest start date last. An event found in two feeds is saved and charged once. Leave one city for a quick first run; set the list empty to search worldwide with a keyword.
categoriesarrayOptional. Luma categories: ai, tech, arts, climate, crypto, fitness, wellness, running, books, games, family, fooddrink. Each category is scraped around each city above (Luma lists category events by location). Several categories = any of them.
querystringOptional keyword searched by Luma in event names and descriptions, e.g. hackathon, founders, yoga, web3. Applied inside each city, category and calendar feed (Luma returns the 50 best matches per feed). With cities set to an empty list and no other source, it searches worldwide.
startUrlsarrayOptional. Any public lu.ma / luma.com link: an organiser calendar (https://lu.ma/planetscale), a single event (https://lu.ma/qjw9i5a9), a city (https://lu.ma/sf) or a category (https://lu.ma/ai); cal-..., evt-..., discplace-... ids too. Calendars return their upcoming events. When only URLs are given, the default city is not scraped.
daysAheadintegerOnly events starting within the next N days (1-365), e.g. 7 for this week's events. Leave empty for all upcoming events (feeds are ordered by start date, so maxEvents takes the soonest ones).
startDateFromstringOptional earliest start date, YYYY-MM-DD or ISO date-time (UTC), e.g. 2026-11-01. Applied by Luma's own date cursor, so later pages are not fetched for nothing.
startDateTostringOptional latest start date, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive) or ISO date-time. Each feed stops at the first event after this date.
priceTypestringany (default), free (ticket price 0 / no ticket) or paid (at least one paid ticket type). Checked on every event before it is saved or charged.
eventFormatstringany (default), in-person (events with a physical venue) or online (no venue or a meeting link as the venue, incl. events whose location is not announced).
includeDetailsbooleanOn (default): one extra request per new event adds the full description (plain text and HTML), every public ticket type with its price, the event's Luma categories and the sold-out flag. The price per event is the same either way. Off: feed fields only (name, dates, venue, GPS, price range, hosts, calendar, guest count), roughly twice as fast.
maxEventsintegerStop after this many saved events (default 25). Cost: $0.0015 per event with details, so 25 events = $0.04. A city has 50-150 upcoming events; raise this for full exports.
maxEventsPerSourceintegerOptional cap per feed so one busy city does not use up maxEvents (0 = no cap).
onlyNewSinceLastRunbooleanOn: deliver only events that an earlier run with the same stateName has not already delivered, and skip the rest without charging. Off (default): return every matching event.
stateNamestringOptional name for this search's memory when onlyNewSinceLastRun is on, e.g. sf-ai-daily. Leave empty to derive it from the cities, categories, keyword and URLs. Use a new key to start over.
skipEventIdsarrayEvent ids you already have (the id field from earlier runs, e.g. evt-Dgnnl0IoUmK5Se1; lu.ma/<slug> URLs are accepted too). Skipped before any detail fetch and never charged. Large lists are fine.

Price
$0.0015 per event ($1.50 per 1,000); $0.001 per run. List prices for Apify Free and Starter plans; Scale and Business plans pay 15% to 30% less.
EventPricePer 1,000Charged when
Event$0.0015$1.50One Luma event saved to the dataset: id, URL, name, start/end (UTC + local + timezone), in-person/online, venue, address, city, region, country, GPS, free/paid, price range and currency, sold-out, spots remaining, approval, guest count, organiser calendar (name, URL, website, socials), hosts (name, bio, profile URL, website, LinkedIn/X/Instagram handles), categories, cover image, full description (text + HTML) and ticket types. Details included in the price; skipped or filtered events are never charged.
Actor Start$0.001Charged when the Actor starts running. Number of events charged depends on Actor memory (one event per GB, minimum one event).
Worked example: the input above, capped at 50 events, costs at most $0.076. Apify's free plan includes $5 of usage a month, about 3,333 events; the Actor's own compute is included in the per-record price, and records skipped by filters, de-duplication or only-new mode are not charged.

What it is not for
Eventbrite, Meetup (not covered); attendee or guest lists (never collected). The data belongs to its publisher; the Actor reads public pages and endpoints and leaves out personal contact details.

Ready-made example pages
Saved inputs you can run with one click on Apify (Examples tab); each has its own page:
Tech events in San Francisco this week (Luma): Every Luma (lu.ma) Tech-category event in and around San Francisco starting in the next 7 days, with venue, GPS, prices, hosts, organiser calendar and full description. Save it as your own task and schedule it weekly. {"cities": ["San Francisco"], "categories": ["tech"], "daysAhead": 7, "maxEvents": 100}
AI events in London - next 30 days (Luma): Upcoming Luma (lu.ma) AI events in and around London over the next 30 days: meetups, hackathons, talks and workshops with venue, GPS, free/paid, hosts with LinkedIn/X handles and full descriptions. {"cities": ["London"], "categories": ["ai"], "daysAhead": 30, "maxEvents": 100}
Startup & tech events in Bengaluru (Bangalore) - Luma: Upcoming Luma (lu.ma) Tech and AI events in Bengaluru (Bangalore): founder meetups, demo days, hackathons and builder nights with venue, GPS, prices, hosts and organiser calendars. {"cities": ["Bengaluru"], "categories": ["tech", "ai"], "maxEvents": 100}
Luma (lu.ma) events in New York, next 14 days, as JSON: Upcoming public events on Luma in New York over the next two weeks with date, venue, hosts, ticket types and prices, as JSON or CSV. Change the city or add categories such as ai, tech or crypto. {"cities": ["New York"], "daysAhead": 14, "includeDetails": true, "maxEvents": 50}

Questions buyers ask
How much does it cost to scrape Luma?
$0.0015 per event with its full details plus $0.001 per run, so 100 events cost about $0.15 and a daily feed of 20 new events about $1 a month.
Is there an official Luma API?
Luma has a paid API for calendar owners (their own events). This Actor reads the public JSON that the lu.ma website itself loads for discover, category, calendar and event pages, and exposes it as a REST API with schedules, webhooks and only-new runs. No login or API key is needed.
Does it collect attendees or guest lists?
No. The Actor never requests or outputs guest lists, guest names, e-mails or phone numbers, including the "N going" avatars shown on event pages. It outputs the hosts' and organiser calendar's public profile information exactly as the event page shows it (name, bio, profile URL, website and social handles).
Why is the address missing on some events?
Hosts can show the exact address only to registered guests. Luma then shows the city and neighbourhood, and so does the Actor: address and venue are null, addressHidden is true, and the coordinates are rounded to about 1 km. City, region and country are still filled in.
Why does an online-only run of a city return nothing?
Luma's city and category pages list events with a physical location near that city. Online events are found through organiser calendars (startUrls) and keyword searches with cities: [], and are marked format: "online".
Which cities and categories exist?
The 87 cities on lu.ma/discover (any lu.ma/<city> page; the Actor also resolves new cities live) and the 12 categories ai, tech, arts, climate, crypto, fitness, wellness, running, books, games, family, fooddrink. A city or category Luma does not know ends the run with Saved 0 events and the known examples in the status message.
Can I scrape past events?
Not in this version: Luma's public feeds list upcoming events. Open an issue if you need an organiser's past events.
Does it work for luma.com links?
Yes. lu.ma and luma.com are the same site; paste either form in startUrls.

Alternatives, honestly
OptionWhat it gives youWhere it falls short for this job
Luma website and iCal feedsBrowse; subscribe to one calendarNo cross-city export, no host profiles in bulk
Eventbrite or Meetup ActorsOther event platformsDifferent events; this API reads Luma only
Other Luma Actors on Apify StoreSame sourceCompare detail fields (hosts, tickets, GPS) and price per 1,000

Published by Daemon Data (data_daemon on Apify Store). Prices, fields and example pages on this page were read from the live Apify listing on 2026-10-29; the listing is the canonical description of the Actor.

Input and how to call it

A verified example input (it returned data on 2026-10-29):

{
  "cities": [
    "Pune"
  ],
  "departments": [
    "Delivery / Driver / Logistics"
  ],
  "postedWithin": "7d",
  "maxJobsPerSearch": 50
}

One HTTP call starts a run, waits for it and returns the records (token from console.apify.com):

curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/data_daemon~apna-jobs-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"cities": ["Pune"], "departments": ["Delivery / Driver / Logistics"], "postedWithin": "7d", "maxJobsPerSearch": 50}'

Python: ApifyClient(token).actor("data_daemon/apna-jobs-scraper").call(run_input=...), full file python/apna-jobs-scraper.py. Node.js: node/apna-jobs-scraper.mjs. n8n: importable workflow.
AI assistant (MCP): add the remote server https://mcp.apify.com/?tools=data_daemon/apna-jobs-scraper with header Authorization: Bearer YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN in Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or VS Code and ask for the data in plain words.

All input fields
FieldTypeMeaning
searchTermsarrayJob titles or skills, e.g. telecaller, delivery boy, accountant, python developer, driver. One Apna search per keyword; Apna returns at most 500 jobs per keyword. Leave empty for the latest jobs, filtered by city, department and the options below.
allJobsbooleanIgnore the keywords and export every open Apna job, department by department (about 71,000 of the 76,800 open jobs on 26 Oct 2026 carry a department). Combine with Only new jobs since the last run for a daily feed, or with cities / departments to export a slice. Large: set a maximum cost per run.
citiesarrayCity names, e.g. Mumbai, Delhi, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai, Kolkata, Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Lucknow. Apna filters by 74 cities; Delhi, Gurgaon, Noida and Ghaziabad all map to Delhi-NCR. Other place names are matched against each job's location. remote means work from home.
departmentsarrayApna departments, e.g. Sales & BD, Customer Support, Delivery / Driver / Logistics, Software Engineering, Finance & Accounting, Healthcare / Doctor / Hospital Staff, Banking / Insurance / Financial Services. A word such as sales, delivery or healthcare picks the matching department. Applies to runs without keywords.
workModesarrayOnly jobs with these work modes. Empty = any.
workTypestringOnly full-time or only part-time jobs.
shiftstringOnly day-shift or only night-shift jobs.
educationstringJobs open to candidates with this highest education, as Apna filters them.
englishLevelstringJobs open to candidates with this English level, as Apna filters them.
postedWithinstringOnly jobs posted or refreshed by the employer recently (Apna's own windows; a refreshed job keeps its original postedAt). Last 24 hours with All jobs is a daily board-wide feed of about 2,000 jobs on an average day.
includeDescriptionbooleanFull job description as plain text. Keyword searches fetch each job page for it (slower); the feed already carries it. Price is the same either way.
maxJobsPerSearchintegerCap for each keyword (or each city / department listing). 0 = no cap. Not used with All jobs.
maxJobsintegerStop after this many saved jobs. 0 or empty = no total cap (the run's maximum cost still applies).
onlyNewSinceLastRunbooleanFor schedules: remember delivered job ids (in a named key-value store in your account) and save only jobs that earlier runs with the same settings did not deliver. Skipped jobs are not charged.
stateNamestringName of the only-new memory. Empty = derived from the keywords and filters. Give two schedules the same name to share one memory.
skipJobIdsarrayApna job ids you already have (the id field). They are neither saved nor charged.

Price
$0.0008 per job ($0.80 per 1,000); $0.001 per run. List prices for Apify Free and Starter plans; Scale and Business plans pay 15% to 30% less.

Skipped or filtered jobs are never charged.
Actor Start$0.001Charged when the Actor starts running. Number of events charged depends on Actor memory (one event per GB, minimum one event).

Questions buyers ask
Is there an official Apna API?
Not a public one. This Actor reads the public JSON job feed and job pages that the apna.co website loads. It exposes them as a REST API with schedules, webhooks and only-new runs.
Does it return candidates or recruiter contacts?
No. It returns job listings only: no candidate data, and no recruiter names, phone numbers or e-mail addresses.
Why do some jobs have no salary?
The employer did not disclose it, or the job is an external listing applied for on the employer's own career site.
Do I need a proxy or login?
No.

experienceYearsintegerOnly jobs whose experience range covers this many years, e.g. 2 keeps "1 to 3 Yrs" and "0 to 4 Yrs" but not "5 to 8 Yrs".
postedWithinDaysintegerOnly jobs posted in the last N days (e.g. 1 for a daily feed). Results are read newest first, so the search stops at the first page of older jobs. 0 or empty = any date.
includeDescriptionbooleanOpen each job page for the full description (text + HTML), numeric salary range, industry, function, employment type and expiry date. Turn off for a fast list of titles, companies, cities, experience, salary text and skills. Price is the same either way.
maxJobsPerSearchintegerCap for each keyword (and city). Newest jobs come first. 0 = no cap (a popular keyword can have tens of thousands of jobs; set a maximum cost per run).
maxJobsintegerStop after this many saved jobs. 0 or empty = no total cap (the run's maximum cost still applies).
onlyNewSinceLastRunbooleanFor schedules: remember delivered job ids (in a named key-value store in your account) and save only jobs that earlier runs with the same settings did not deliver. Skipped jobs are not charged.
stateNamestringName of the only-new memory. Empty = derived from the keywords, cities and experience. Give two schedules the same name to share one memory.
skipJobIdsarrayShine job ids you already have (the id field). They are neither fetched, saved nor charged.

The employer chose "Not Disclosed". salaryText then says so.
Do I need a proxy?

All input fields
FieldTypeMeaning
opportunityTypesarrayUnstop listing types. Each type is one search; a listing is saved and charged once. On 26 Oct 2026 Unstop had about 710 open jobs, 570 internships, 670 competitions, 210 hackathons, 110 workshops, 75 quizzes and 5 scholarships.
searchTermsarrayOptional. Unstop matches them against listing titles and organisation names, e.g. data analyst, marketing, software engineer, Reliance. Each keyword runs once per type. Leave empty to get every open listing of the chosen types.
workplaceTypesarrayOnly jobs and internships with these workplace types. Empty = any.
timingstringOnly full-time or only part-time jobs and internships.
paystringMostly useful for internships: paid (with a stipend) or unpaid.
eligibilitystringOnly listings open to this group, as set by the organiser.
modestringOnly online or only in-person events.
entryFeestringOnly free or only paid-entry events.
postedWithinDaysintegerOnly listings published on Unstop in the last N days (e.g. 1 for a daily feed, 7 for weekly). 0 or empty = any date.
locationsarrayOnly listings whose city, state or country contains one of these words, e.g. Bangalore, Mumbai, Maharashtra. remote matches work-from-home jobs. Listings without a location (many online events) are left out when this is set.
includeDescriptionbooleanFull description as plain text (description) and HTML (descriptionHtml). It costs the same either way; turn it off for smaller files.
maxResultsPerSearchintegerCap for each type (and keyword). Newest listings come first. 0 = no cap: every open listing, about 2,350 across all types.
maxResultsintegerStop after this many saved listings. 0 or empty = no total cap (the run's maximum cost still applies).
onlyNewSinceLastRunbooleanFor schedules: remember delivered listing ids (in a named key-value store in your account) and save only listings that earlier runs with the same settings did not deliver. Skipped listings are not charged.
stateNamestringName of the only-new memory. Empty = derived from the types, keywords and filters. Give two schedules the same name to share one memory.
skipIdsarrayUnstop listing ids you already have (the id field). They are neither saved nor charged.

Price
$0.0015 per opportunity ($1.50 per 1,000); $0.001 per run. List prices for Apify Free and Starter plans; Scale and Business plans pay 15% to 30% less.
EventPricePer 1,000Charged when
Opportunity$0.0015$1.50One Unstop listing saved to the dataset (job, internship, hackathon, competition, quiz, workshop or scholarship): id, URL, title, organiser, locations, workplace type, salary or stipend, eligibility, skills, registration dates and deadline, team size, entry fee, prizes, registration and view counts, and the full description (text + HTML). Skipped or filtered listings are never charged.
Actor Start$0.001Charged when the Actor starts running. Number of events charged depends on Actor memory (one event per GB, minimum one event).
Worked example: the input above, capped at 50 opportunitys, costs at most $0.076. Apify's free plan includes $5 of usage a month, about 3,333 opportunitys; the Actor's own compute is included in the per-record price, and records skipped by filters, de-duplication or only-new mode are not charged.

Ready-made example pages
Saved inputs you can run with one click on Apify (Examples tab); each has its own page:
Open hackathons in India on Unstop (live list): Hackathons currently open for registration on Unstop: title, organiser, prize pool, registration deadline, team size, eligibility (students, freshers, professionals), online or offline, city, entry fee and the full descr {"opportunityTypes": ["hackathons"], "includeDescription": true, "maxResultsPerSearch": 100}
Paid work-from-home internships on Unstop: Paid internships that can be done from home, listed on Unstop: role, company, stipend, skills, eligibility, start and end dates, application deadline and the full description. Newest first. Useful for students, placement {"opportunityTypes": ["internships"], "workplaceTypes": ["wfh"], "pay": "paid", "includeDescription": true, "maxResultsPerSearch": 100}

Questions buyers ask
Is there an official Unstop API?
Unstop does not offer a documented public API. This Actor reads the public JSON endpoints (/api/public/opportunity/...) that the unstop.com website loads, which robots.txt allows. It exposes them as a REST API with schedules, webhooks and only-new runs.
Does it return closed listings?
No. It returns listings that are open for registration, which is what Unstop shows by default.
Does it include participants or applicant details?
No. It returns listing data only: the organiser, the role or event, deadlines and counts. No personal data about candidates or participants is collected.
Why does a salary show as empty?
The organiser chose not to disclose it. About 80% of jobs and internships show a salary or stipend.
Do I need a proxy or login?
No.

# Dubai Land Department transactions as JSON: registered sold prices, weekly volumes and how to pull them

Source: https://datadmon.github.io/guides/dubai-land-department-transactions-json/

The Dubai Land Department (DLD) publishes every registered property transaction in Dubai as open data: each sale, off-plan pre-registration, mortgage registration and gift, with the transaction date, the value in AED, the area and project, property type, rooms, parking and size. It is the only source of **actual registered prices** for Dubai; listing portals show asking prices. This guide explains what the register contains, how much data it produces and how to pull it as JSON.

## What a week of DLD data looks like (measured 11 to 18 October 2026)

| Transaction group | Transactions per week | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Sales | about 2,600 | 1,650 off-plan (developer pre-registrations), 950 ready properties |
| Mortgages | about 1,300 | registrations and modifications, separated by the `procedure` field |
| Gifts | about 160 | transfers between family members |
| Land plots | about 220 of the sales | `propertyType: "land"` |
| **Total** | **about 4,100** | a typical week is 3,000 to 6,000 |

Roughly 2,500 of the 2,600 weekly sales are residential; the rest are commercial.

## Fields in each record

Every record carries the transaction date (ISO), transaction number, `procedure` (for example `Sale`, `Delayed Sell`, `Sell - Pre registration`, mortgage registration or modification), transaction group, property type and sub-type, usage (residential or commercial), area and project names (a master project only on the rare rows where DLD names one, under 1%), rooms, parking, actual area in square metres, value in AED and a precomputed `pricePerSqmAed`, plus boolean off-plan and freehold flags. Arabic names are available as an optional object. The register contains no owner names or contact details.

## Free portals versus the register as data

Dubai Pulse (the government open-data portal) and DXB Interact (DLD's dashboard) let you look up transactions and download extracts by hand. They are the right tools for a one-off question. They are the wrong tools for a daily feed into a database, a valuation model that needs price per square metre by project, or an app that shows registered prices next to listings, because each extract is manual and the files need cleaning. The Daemon Data API reads the same DLD open-data service, pages through the whole date range 500 rows at a time and returns analysis-ready records.

## How to pull it

One call returns last week's residential unit sales (about 2,500 rows, about $2.50):

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/data_daemon~dubai-property-transactions/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"daysBack": 7, "transactionGroup": "sales", "usage": "residential", "propertyType": "unit", "maxItems": 0}'
```

For a daily feed, save the input with `daysBack: 1` as a task and schedule it; the ready-made example page "Dubai DLD property transactions, last 24 hours, as JSON" returned 1,000 transactions in 6 seconds on 21 October 2026. For a date range use `fromDate` and `toDate` (`YYYY-MM-DD`). To filter by area, read the `area` and `project` fields of the output; the service's own area id filter returns no rows at present.

## What it costs

$1 per 1,000 transactions, nothing else. A month of all sales (about 11,000 rows) costs about $11; a weekly residential feed about $2.50 a week; a daily feed of everything about $17 a month. Apify's free plan includes $5 of usage every month.

## Questions and answers

**Is this official Dubai Land Department data?**

Yes. The API reads the Dubai Land Department's own open-data transactions service, the same register that paid DLD data products resell. It is published by the department for reuse.

**Are these asking prices or sold prices?**

Registered transaction values, that is what buyers actually paid or what was registered for a mortgage or gift. Asking prices come from listing portals and are not in the register.

**How do I tell an off-plan pre-registration from a completed sale?**

Use the `procedure` field: `Sell - Pre registration` is a developer pre-registration, `Sale` and `Delayed Sell` are completed sales. The `offPlan` input filter and the boolean flag in each record do the same split.

**Does the register include owner names?**

No. The open-data service carries no personal data, and the API adds none.

**How far back can I go?**

Any date range the DLD service holds; the input accepts `fromDate` and `toDate`, or `daysBack` up to 365.

# How to export every IIMJobs and Hirist job as a daily feed

Source: https://datadmon.github.io/guides/iimjobs-hirist-full-board-job-feed/

Job aggregators, HR-tech products and hiring-market trackers usually need **all** of a job board, not the results of a few keywords. IIMJobs.com (MBA, finance, consulting, sales, HR and senior management roles in India) and Hirist.tech (India's tech-only board) have no public export. Since 26 October 2026 the **IIMJobs Jobs Scraper** and the **Hirist.tech Jobs Scraper** on Apify can deliver every listing a board shows in a date window, with the same fields as a keyword search.

## How much there is

Measured on 26 October 2026 with the boards' own date filters:

| Board | Jobs posted in the last 7 days | Last 30 days |
|---|---:|---:|
| IIMJobs | 1,199 (about 170 a day) | 4,602 |
| Hirist | 959 (about 140 a day) | 4,448 |

Weekends are quieter: on a Sunday IIMJobs showed 17 new listings.

## Step 1: run the full board once

Open the [IIMJobs Jobs Scraper](https://apify.com/data_daemon/iimjobs-jobs-scraper) (or the [Hirist.tech Jobs Scraper](https://apify.com/data_daemon/hirist-jobs-scraper)), switch on **All jobs on the board** and run it with:

```json
{
  "allJobs": true,
  "postedWithinDays": 3,
  "onlyNewSinceLastRun": true,
  "stateName": "iimjobs-full-board"
}
```

The Actor ignores the keywords and walks every listing posted in the window, newest first. Each row has the job ID, title, company (with industry, size and AmbitionBox rating when available), locations, experience range, salary in LPA when disclosed, skills, applicant and view counts, posting time and the full job description. `locations`, the experience range and `maxJobs` still apply if you only want part of the board. Putting `*` in the keywords does the same as the switch.

## Step 2: schedule it daily

Create a daily Apify schedule for the run (or a saved task with this input). Because of **only-new mode**, every later run returns only jobs the feed named by `stateName` has not delivered yet; repeats are skipped and not charged. We checked this on 26 October 2026: two back-to-back runs returned 15 and then 2 jobs, with no job delivered twice.

The date window counts calendar days in India time. Three days is a safe window for a daily schedule: it covers weekends and a run that starts late, and only-new mode removes the overlap.

## Step 3: load it where you need it

The dataset of each run is available as JSON, CSV or Excel through the Apify API, so a database loader, an n8n or Make workflow, or a Google Sheets import can pick it up. Key on `dedupKey` (for example `iimjobs:1741775`), which is stable across runs and boards.

## The same switch on Foundit and Instahyre

The [Foundit Jobs Scraper](https://apify.com/data_daemon/foundit-jobs-scraper) and the [Instahyre Jobs Scraper](https://apify.com/data_daemon/instahyre-jobs-scraper) have the same **All jobs on the board** option. foundit (formerly Monster India) is far busier: **2,815 jobs posted in the last day** on 26 October 2026, so its window defaults to one day. Instahyre had **12,724 open jobs** and no date filter on the site, so follow it with only-new mode alone: the first run exports the open jobs (about 80 minutes at roughly three jobs a second; it stops cleanly before the run timeout and the next run continues), and later runs return only jobs that are new to the feed.

## Costs and limits

Each Actor charges per job saved, with the price shown on its Apify pricing tab; jobs skipped by only-new mode are free. A board-wide daily feed is roughly the number of new jobs per day from the table above. Set **Maximum cost per run** on the schedule if you want a hard ceiling; the run stops cleanly at that limit and says so.

# How to get new IIMJobs postings in Google Sheets every morning

Source: https://datadmon.github.io/guides/iimjobs-new-jobs-google-sheets/

Recruiters, career coaches and hiring-market analysts who follow **IIMJobs.com** usually want one thing: the jobs that appeared since yesterday, in a spreadsheet, without copying them by hand and without seeing the same posting twice. IIMJobs has no public API or export, so this guide sets up a daily feed with the **IIMJobs Jobs Scraper** on Apify and a free n8n workflow that writes the rows to Google Sheets and posts a summary to Slack.

## What you get in each row

Every job comes back as one row with the job ID, title, company (name, industry, size and AmbitionBox rating when available), locations, experience range, salary in LPA when the recruiter discloses it, skills, applicant count, posting date, the public job URL and, if you switch it on, the full job description. Most IIMJobs recruiters hide pay, so a `salaryHidden` flag tells you which rows have none.

Demand is large enough to make a feed worthwhile: a `product manager` search matched 4,097 open IIMJobs listings and `investment banking` 652 when we measured them between 18 and 21 October 2026.

## Step 1: run the Actor once with only-new mode

Open the [IIMJobs Jobs Scraper on Apify](https://apify.com/data_daemon/iimjobs-jobs-scraper), click **Try for free** and paste this input:

```json
{
  "queries": ["product manager", "investment banking"],
  "onlyNewSinceLastRun": true,
  "stateName": "my-daily-feed",
  "maxJobs": 100
}
```

`onlyNewSinceLastRun` makes the Actor remember which job IDs this feed (named by `stateName`) has already delivered. The next run returns only jobs it has not sent before, and **skipped repeats are not charged**. We checked this on 23 October 2026: two back-to-back runs with the same feed name returned six different jobs and no repeats.

## Step 2: schedule it

In Apify Console open **Schedules**, create a daily schedule (for example 08:00 in Asia/Kolkata) and add the Actor run or a saved task with the input above. Each morning the dataset of that run contains only the new postings.

## Step 3: send the rows to Google Sheets and Slack with n8n

If you use [n8n](https://n8n.io), import the ready workflow [iimjobs-new-jobs-to-google-sheets-and-slack.json](https://github.com/datadmon/apify-data-actors-examples/blob/main/n8n/iimjobs-new-jobs-to-google-sheets-and-slack.json). It runs at 08:00, calls the Actor through the Apify API with only-new mode, **upserts** each job into a `Jobs` tab (matched on `id`, so re-runs never duplicate rows) and posts the count and the first five jobs to a Slack channel. Setup:

1. Create an n8n *Header Auth* credential named `Authorization` with the value `Bearer YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN` (Apify Console → Settings → API & Integrations).
2. Connect Google Sheets and paste your sheet URL. Add a `Jobs` tab with the header row `id, title, company, locations, experience, salaryLpa, skills, applicants, postedAt, url`.
3. Connect Slack, pick a channel, edit the `queries` and activate the workflow.

The request URL already carries `maxTotalChargeUsd=0.5`, a hard cost cap per run.

Prefer code? The same feed is a few lines of Python with the official `apify-client` package; a complete example is in the [examples repository](https://github.com/datadmon/apify-data-actors-examples/tree/main/examples/only-new-jobs).

## Tips

- **One feed per question.** Use a separate `stateName` for each search you track, for example `pm-mumbai` and `ib-all-india`. Changing the queries under the same name mixes their memory.
- **Narrow the first run.** The first run delivers a capped baseline of open jobs; later runs add only the new ones. Add `"postedWithinDays": 1` if you never want older postings.
- **Tech roles instead?** Point the same workflow at `data_daemon~hirist-jobs-scraper`; the input and output fields are the same.
- **Cost.** Both Actors are pay-per-result with a free trial; the current price is on each Apify page.

## FAQ

**Is there an official IIMJobs API?** No public one. The Actor reads the job data the IIMJobs website itself loads, needs no login, cookies or proxy, and returns it as JSON, CSV, Excel or rows in your sheet.

**Does it collect recruiter contact details?** No. Recruiter names and phone numbers are left out on purpose; the recruiter's designation is kept only where IIMJobs shows it to every visitor.

**Can I get alerts in Microsoft Teams or email instead of Slack?** Yes: replace the Slack node in n8n with a Teams or Gmail node. Make and Zapier can call the same Apify Actor as well.

# India IPO GMP and subscription data as JSON: what the numbers mean and how to get them

Source: https://datadmon.github.io/guides/india-ipo-gmp-subscription-data-json/

Indian IPO coverage runs on two numbers that no exchange publishes: the **grey market premium (GMP)**, the unofficial price at which IPO shares change hands before listing, and the **subscription multiple**, how many times each investor category has bid for the shares on offer. Both are published by independent IPO sites and change many times a day while an issue is open. This guide explains what the figures mean, where they come from and how to pull them, together with the IPO calendar and listing results, as structured JSON.

## The figures, explained

- **GMP (grey market premium)**: the premium in rupees over the issue price that grey-market traders quote for the shares before listing, also expressed as a percentage. It is an unofficial indicator of listing-day sentiment, not an exchange figure and not investment advice. The report also carries the estimated listing price and the IPO's status (upcoming, open, closing today, closed, listing today, listed above or below the issue price).
- **Subscription**: the number of times the shares reserved for each category were bid for, as published by BSE and NSE: QIB (qualified institutional buyers), NII split into small and big non-institutional investors, retail, employee and shareholder quotas, and the total, plus application counts.
- **Calendar**: open, close, allotment, refund and listing dates for every upcoming issue, day by day, with exchange holidays marked.
- **Listing performance and GMP performance**: issue price versus listing-day open and close and the current price, and the last GMP before listing versus the actual listing price, which is the data for "how accurate was the GMP".
- **IPO list and details**: every mainboard and SME IPO of the year with issue size, fresh and offer-for-sale split, lead manager, ISIN, BSE scrip code and NSE symbol, and an optional full detail page per IPO (reservation, anchor investors, financials, valuation, objects of the issue).

## Volumes (measured 18 October 2026)

A live GMP report has about 30 to 50 rows (every upcoming, open and recently listed IPO), the calendar about 30, and the year-to-date subscription, IPO-list, current-IPO and listing-performance reports about 280 to 300 rows each. GMP moves most during bidding hours (9:00 to 15:30 IST) and is worth polling every 30 minutes then; the calendar changes daily.

## How to pull it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/data_daemon~india-ipo-tracker/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"reports": ["gmp", "subscription"], "category": "all"}'
```

Every record carries the same stable `slug` (for example `paras-healthcare-ipo`), so GMP, subscription, calendar and listing rows join without fuzzy name matching; subscription, list and listing rows also carry ISIN and exchange symbols for joining to a security master. The `category` filter restricts to mainboard or SME issues. Runs finish in under 30 seconds.

## What it costs

$3 per 1,000 report rows and $15 per 1,000 IPO detail pages. The default run (live GMP plus calendar, about 80 rows) costs about $0.25; a full year-to-date snapshot with subscription and current IPOs about $2; a broker app polling GMP every 30 minutes during bidding hours about $2 per trading day.

## Questions and answers

**What is the grey market premium of an IPO?**

The unofficial premium over the issue price at which IPO shares are traded before listing, quoted by grey-market dealers and published by IPO tracking sites. A GMP of ₹60 on a ₹300 issue price means dealers expect a listing near ₹360 (20%). It is sentiment, not a guarantee, and the GMP-performance report shows how often it was right.

**Where does the subscription data come from?**

From the bid data BSE and NSE publish while an issue is open, as compiled by the IPO report sites the API reads. The API returns QIB, sNII, bNII, NII, retail, employee, shareholder and total multiples plus application counts.

**Does it cover SME IPOs?**

Yes, mainboard and SME issues on both exchanges, with a `category` filter for either.

**Is there an official API for GMP?**

No. Exchanges do not publish grey-market data. Official broker APIs (for example Upstox's) publish the IPO calendar and some subscription figures, but not GMP; this API joins GMP and subscription in one feed with a common key.

**How accurate is GMP as a forecast of the listing price?**

For the 294 IPOs listed from 2 January to 28 October 2026, the last GMP before listing missed the actual listing gain by 8.6 percentage points on average (7.0 for mainboard, 9.6 for SME issues); 69% listed within 10 points of their GMP, and no IPO with a GMP above 25% listed below its issue price. Method and bands: [How accurate is IPO GMP? We checked all 294 Indian IPOs listed in 2026](https://dev.to/datadaemon/how-accurate-is-ipo-gmp-we-checked-all-294-indian-ipos-listed-in-2026-4bdg).

**Is this investment advice?**

No. GMP is an unofficial indicator; the data is provided for information and research.


---

# India job board data compared: IIMJobs, Hirist, Foundit and Instahyre as APIs

Source: https://datadmon.github.io/guides/india-job-boards-data-compared/

India has no single job board. Recruiters post management roles on IIMJobs, software roles on Hirist, mass-market and syndicated roles on foundit (formerly Monster India) and product-company tech roles on Instahyre, and none of the four offers a public API. This guide compares the four boards as **data sources**: what each one covers, which fields it exposes, how fresh the postings are and what it costs to pull them through the Daemon Data APIs on Apify. All counts were measured on 18 to 21 October 2026 with the APIs themselves.

## Coverage, measured

| Board | What it lists | Size signal (Oct 2026) | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **IIMJobs** | Management, consulting, finance, CA/CFA, sales, marketing, HR and MBA-track roles, 2 to 25 years of experience | `product manager` matched 4,097 open listings; `investment banking` 652 | Senior and mid-management hiring, salary benchmarks, who-is-hiring signals |
| **Hirist** | Software, data, DevOps and product-tech roles at IT companies and startups | `data engineer` 3,420 open jobs (239 posted in the last 7 days); `python developer` 1,884 | Tech recruiting, skills demand, tech salary bands |
| **foundit** | Every function and level: IT, sales, BPO, nursing, accounting, operations, freshers; many postings syndicated from employers' career sites | about 223,000 open listings and 2,900 new postings a day; `data analyst` 1,192 | Volume, freshers, non-tech roles, employer apply links |
| **Instahyre** | Engineering, data, product and design roles at Indian product companies and startups, curated by the platform | 12,743 open jobs: 6,764 in Bangalore, 1,700 Gurgaon, 1,228 Hyderabad, 1,095 work from home; `python` 4,300 | Startup hiring signals, company-size filters, remote tech roles |

## Fields: what each board gives you

| Field | IIMJobs | Hirist | foundit | Instahyre |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Full job description (HTML and text) | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Salary band | when the recruiter discloses it (INR LPA) | when disclosed | when disclosed; `salaryHidden` flag | not published by the site |
| Applicant and view counts | yes | yes | yes | not published |
| Experience range | yes | yes | yes | yes (from the job page) |
| Company profile | AmbitionBox profile when one exists | AmbitionBox profile | name, logo, employer vs staffing agency, GPTW flag | name, tagline, founding year, headcount, size band, website, logo |
| Skills tags | yes | yes | yes, with the site's normalised IT-skill tags | yes |
| Recruiter contact | not output (privacy) | not output | not output | not output |
| Posting date | exact timestamp | exact timestamp | exact timestamp; reposts refresh it | day precision; jobs stay open for months |
| Apply link | board page | board page | employer's own site for syndicated jobs | board page |

## Freshness and feeds

IIMJobs, Hirist and foundit let the API ask the site for postings from the last N days, so a daily feed is cheap: a `postedWithinDays: 1` run only touches new jobs. Instahyre's search has no date filter, so the API reads the posting date from each job page; in practice you run it in **only-new mode**, where the API remembers the job ids it has already delivered (in a key-value store in your own Apify account) and later runs return only what is new on the site. All four APIs share that only-new mode, the `skipJobIds` field and the same `queries` / `locations` input, so one pipeline can read all four boards.

### Start an IIMJobs feed with a total cap

Use a distinct `stateName` for each saved search. This input delivers at most 50 jobs across all keywords, including the first run:

```json
{
  "queries": ["product manager"],
  "postedWithinDays": 3,
  "onlyNewSinceLastRun": true,
  "stateName": "product-manager-daily",
  "maxJobsPerQuery": 50,
  "maxJobs": 50
}
```

At the FREE-tier list price, a 50-job run with descriptions costs at most $0.20 through 1 November 2026, then $0.101 including the start fee from 2 November. Later runs skip jobs already delivered; they may still return unseen jobs from the three-day window that exceeded a previous run's cap. A quiet search can return zero rows successfully.

**Verified 22 October 2026:** two consecutive runs on IIMJobs build 0.2.11, using this input shape with both caps reduced to 3, returned six distinct jobs. The second run reported three previously delivered jobs skipped. This verifies de-duplication, not a promise of three new postings between calls.

For code, use the [Python and Node only-new-jobs examples](https://github.com/datadmon/apify-data-actors-examples/tree/main/examples/only-new-jobs) or the [n8n workflow for Google Sheets and Slack](https://github.com/datadmon/apify-data-actors-examples/blob/main/n8n/iimjobs-new-jobs-to-google-sheets-and-slack.json). For Console setup, save the input as a task and choose your timezone explicitly when adding a schedule.

## Price per 1,000 jobs (FREE-plan list prices, October 2026)

| Board | Price |
|---|---|
| IIMJobs | $2 per 1,000 jobs plus $2 per 1,000 descriptions until 1 November 2026; from 2 November 2026 $2 per 1,000 jobs with the description included, plus $0.001 per run |
| Hirist | same as IIMJobs |
| foundit | $0.80 per 1,000 jobs, description included, plus $0.001 per run |
| Instahyre | $0.80 per 1,000 jobs, description included, plus $0.001 per run |

A 50-job daily feed therefore costs between about $1.25 and $6 a month depending on the board. Jobs skipped by only-new mode or by your filters are never charged.

## Which board for which question

- **"Which companies are hiring finance or product leaders in India this week?"** IIMJobs; filter on experience and read the applicant counts to see which mandates are crowded.
- **"What skills do Indian tech employers ask for, and what do they pay?"** Hirist for skills: every row carries skill tags, split into mandatory and nice-to-have. Pay is rarer than the skills: Hirist showed a salary band on 10 of 170 new jobs on 28 October 2026 and IIMJobs on 28 of 140, so salary research needs a few weeks of history. Add Instahyre for startup roles with company headcount.
- **"Fresher or non-tech roles, or the largest possible volume."** foundit, with its 2,900 new postings a day and fresher filters by experience band.
- **"Startups and product companies hiring engineers, by company size or remote."** Instahyre, the only board here that publishes employer headcount and founding year and lets you filter by company size.

## Questions and answers

**Is there an official API for IIMJobs, Hirist, foundit or Instahyre?**

No. None of the four publishes a public API. The Daemon Data APIs read the JSON endpoints and public pages the boards' own websites load, and expose them as Apify Actors with schedules, webhooks and only-new runs.

**Which Indian job board shows the salary most often?**

In one day of new postings (24 hours to 28 October 2026): IIMJobs showed a salary on 20% of jobs, Hirist on 6%, foundit on 2%, and Instahyre publishes none. Apna, a frontline board with its own Actor, showed a monthly salary range on every job (median ₹18,000–25,000). Volumes, applicant counts and a script for the daily feed of all five: [One day of Indian job postings: 5,600 new jobs on five boards](https://dev.to/datadaemon/one-day-of-indian-job-postings-5600-new-jobs-on-five-boards-and-how-many-show-the-salary-10nk).

**Can I get the same fields from all four boards in one pipeline?**

Mostly. All four return `id`, `title`, `company.name`, `locations`, `skills`, `postedAt`, `url` and a `description`, and accept the same `queries`, `locations`, `onlyNewSinceLastRun` and `skipJobIds` input. Salary and applicant counts exist on IIMJobs, Hirist and foundit but not on Instahyre; company headcount exists on Instahyre and on Hirist/IIMJobs through AmbitionBox.

**How fresh is the data?**

As fresh as the run: each run reads the live site. The job-board APIs finish a 50-job run in well under a minute. IIMJobs, Hirist and foundit filter by posting date on the server; Instahyre needs only-new mode or a per-job date check.

**Why are recruiter names missing?**

The APIs leave out recruiter names and phone numbers on purpose, even where a board exposes them, and keep the recruiter's designation only where the board shows it to every visitor.


---

# Oracle Recruiting Cloud career sites: how to export every job of an employer as JSON

Source: https://datadmon.github.io/guides/oracle-recruiting-cloud-career-sites-export/

Thousands of large employers run their careers page on **Oracle Recruiting Cloud**, part of Oracle Fusion Cloud HCM: banks, hotel groups, hospitals, universities, manufacturers and governments. Oracle describes the product as helping "organizations enhance the candidate experience, grow talent pools, drive internal mobility, and streamline the hiring process" and lets them "create branded career sites and tailored content for candidates" ([oracle.com](https://www.oracle.com/human-capital-management/recruiting/), accessed 21 October 2026); those branded career sites are the pages this guide is about. These jobs are often posted nowhere else, so job boards, aggregators, talent-intelligence teams and B2B sales teams tracking hiring signals need to read the career sites directly. This guide explains how to recognise such a site, what it exposes and how to export it.

## How to recognise an Oracle Recruiting Cloud career site

The URL contains `oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience`, for example `https://jpmc.fa.oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/CX_1001`. The first part is the employer's tenant, the `sites/CX...` part is the career site number (an employer may run several, for example one per region or one for internal candidates). Every such site is backed by the same JSON endpoints, which is why one API can read any of them.

## Sizes (verified 18 October 2026)

| Employer | Career site | Open jobs |
|---|---|---|
| Kotak Mahindra Bank | `hcbt.fa.em2.oraclecloud.com/.../sites/CX` | 16,521 |
| Marriott International | `ejwl.fa.us2.oraclecloud.com/.../sites/CX` | 13,286 |
| JPMorgan Chase | `jpmc.fa.oraclecloud.com/.../sites/CX_1001` | 7,262 |
| EXL Service | `fa-ewjt-saasfaprod1.fa.ocs.oraclecloud.com/.../sites/CX_2` | 2,841 |
| Oracle | `eeho.fa.us2.oraclecloud.com/.../sites/CX_45001` | 2,372 |
| DTCC | `ebxr.fa.us2.oraclecloud.com/.../sites/CX_1` | 452 |

## What each job record contains

Requisition id (stable across runs), title, posting date, locations, job family and function, workplace type where the employer tags it (remote, hybrid, on-site), the direct apply URL, and with details on: the full description, qualifications, responsibilities, skills and the employer's custom fields. Posting-date filters use Oracle's own two buckets (last 7 days, last 30 days). Keyword and location filters behave like the career site's own search box.

## How to export

Paste any URL from the site, even a single job's URL or just the host name; the API works out the tenant and the employer's active site, and lists the sites that exist if the number is wrong.

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/data_daemon~oracle-hcm-jobs-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"careerSiteUrls": ["https://jpmc.fa.oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/CX_1001"], "location": "India", "postedWithinDays": 7, "includeDetails": true, "maxJobsPerSite": 200}'
```

Several employers go in one list; the ready-made example "Jobs from several Oracle Recruiting Cloud career sites" reads Oracle's and Marriott's sites in one run (80 jobs found in 15 seconds on 21 October 2026). For a daily hiring-signal feed, switch on `onlyNewSinceLastRun`: the API remembers delivered requisition ids per search and later runs return only new postings, without charging for the rest.

## What it costs

$2 per 1,000 jobs plus $2 per 1,000 full detail records, so a 500-job site with details costs $2. Apify's free plan ($5 a month) covers about 1,250 jobs with details. From 2 November 2026 the listing moves to $2 per 1,000 jobs with the details included plus $0.001 per run.

## Questions and answers

**Is there a public API for Oracle Recruiting Cloud job postings?**

Yes, in practice: career sites load their jobs from unauthenticated candidate-experience endpoints (`recruitingCEJobRequisitions`, `recruitingCEJobRequisitionDetails`, `recruitingCESites`). A wrong site number does not fail: on 29 October 2026 Ford's tenant answered `CX_999` with its default site's 915 jobs and Oracle's tenant answered every site number with the same 2,710. Endpoints, parameters and a Python script: [Oracle Recruiting Cloud jobs API](https://dev.to/datadaemon/oracle-recruiting-cloud-jobs-api-the-public-json-endpoints-behind-every-oracle-hcm-career-site-5eal).

**Does this work for Taleo, Workday, Greenhouse or SuccessFactors sites?**

No. It reads Oracle Recruiting Cloud sites only (`oraclecloud.com/hcmUI/CandidateExperience`). Oracle Taleo is a different product with different pages.

**Can I get only new requisitions every morning?**

Yes. Save the input as a task with `onlyNewSinceLastRun: true`, schedule it daily, and connect the task to Slack, Google Sheets or a webhook. Skipped jobs are not charged.

**How do I find the right site number?**

Paste any URL from the employer's careers page. If it has no site number, the API picks the employer's active public site; if the number is retired, the run log lists the sites on that tenant.

**Does it include the employer's internal-only jobs?**

No. It returns what the public career site shows to any visitor.


---

# UK winding-up petitions and insolvency notices as a daily JSON feed from The Gazette

Source: https://datadmon.github.io/guides/uk-winding-up-petitions-daily-feed/

Every UK winding-up petition, winding-up order, administration appointment, liquidation and creditors' meeting must be advertised in The Gazette, usually before the court hearing and weeks before Companies House records the change. That makes the Gazette notice feed the earliest structured signal that a company is in trouble, which is why insolvency practitioners, credit-risk and trade-credit teams, lenders and asset buyers read it daily. This guide explains the volumes, the notice-type codes and how to turn the feed into JSON.

## Volumes (measured for the week of 11 to 17 October 2026)

| Notice type | Gazette code | Per week |
|---|---|---|
| Petitions to wind up a company | 2450 | about 140 (138 that week) |
| Appointment of administrators | 2410 | about 40 (43 that week) |
| Appointment of liquidators | 2432, 2443 | tens |
| Winding-up orders | 2452 | tens |
| Meetings of creditors, notices to creditors | 2442, 2433 | tens |

HMRC is the petitioner in about half of all winding-up petitions (56% of the 620 published in the 30 days to 17 October 2026). Other codes: 2451 petitions against partnerships, 2441 resolutions for winding up, 2503 bankruptcy orders; category `G205000000` is corporate insolvency and `G206000000` personal insolvency.

## What each record contains

The notice itself (title, type, publication date, court, case number, hearing details, petitioner, practitioner firm, notice text and URL) and, with `includeLinkedData` on, the structured record behind it: **company name and number** for joining to Companies House, registered office and trading address, postcode, nature of business and the people and firms named. The Gazette's own data page states that its content, "unless stated otherwise, is Crown Copyright and is therefore free for you to use under the Open Government Licence. However, please note that this licence does not cover the re-use of personal data" ([thegazette.co.uk/data](https://www.thegazette.co.uk/data), accessed 21 October 2026). Its terms add: "All content is available under the Open Government Licence v3.0, except where otherwise stated" ([terms and conditions](https://www.thegazette.co.uk/terms-and-conditions)). Company-level data can therefore be reused with attribution; personal-insolvency notices carry personal data and need separate care.

## How to run a daily feed

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/data_daemon~uk-gazette-insolvency-notices/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"service": "insolvency", "noticeTypes": ["2450", "2410"], "publishedWithinDays": 1, "onlyNewSinceLastRun": true, "includeLinkedData": true, "maxItems": 300}'
```

`publishedWithinDays: 1` is a rolling window counted from today; `onlyNewSinceLastRun` makes the API remember the notice ids it has delivered (for 180 days, in a key-value store in your own Apify account) so a daily schedule returns each notice once and never charges for the rest. Add `text: "Revenue and Customs"` for HMRC petitions only, a town name for a region, or a practitioner firm. The ready-made example "UK corporate insolvency notices, last 48 hours" returned 100 notices with 98 structured records in seconds on 21 October 2026.

## What it costs

$2 per 1,000 notices plus $3 per 1,000 linked-data records, so $5 per 1,000 notices with full structure. A daily petitions feed (about 140 a week) costs about $3 a month; petitions plus administrations plus liquidations about $5 a month; a one-year back-fill of petitions (about 7,000) about $35.

## Questions and answers

**Why read The Gazette instead of Companies House?**

Timing. A winding-up petition is advertised in The Gazette before the hearing; Companies House usually shows the change weeks later, after the order. For early warning the Gazette is the source.

**Which notice codes should a credit team watch?**

2450 (petitions to wind up companies) for the earliest signal, 2410 (administrators appointed) and 2432/2443 (liquidators appointed) for confirmed insolvency, 2452 (winding-up orders) for the court outcome.

**Can I filter to one region or one petitioner?**

Yes. Use the `text` field for a town, a company name, a practitioner firm or `Revenue and Customs`; then filter the output on postcode or address for finer regions.

**Is the data free to reuse?**

Gazette notices are Crown copyright under the Open Government Licence v3.0; reuse company-level data with attribution and handle the personal data in personal-insolvency notices under data-protection law.
